columns.name: CustomerID
columns.description: Unique integer identifier for each customer (one row per CustomerID).
columns.rationale: This is the unique identifier and is marked role=id — it is not a model feature. Keep as an identifier for joins and tracing only.

columns.name: Churn
columns.description: Binary churn label: 1 = customer churned, 0 = retained.
columns.rationale: This is the target label (role=target) with values 0/1. Modelers should treat it as the label to predict; no imputation was done because it's complete.

columns.name: Tenure
columns.description: Customer tenure with the company, measured in months.
columns.rationale: Unit: months. Nullable: null means tenure was not recorded for that customer; missing values were intentionally left for downstream imputation or feature engineering. Range constraint (0–61) ensures no negative or implausible tenures.

columns.name: PreferredLoginDevice
columns.description: Customer's most-used device to log in (Computer or Mobile Phone).
columns.rationale: Allowed values restricted to ['Computer','Mobile Phone'] to avoid spelling variants — canonicalization was applied. This is a categorical feature; handle with appropriate encoding.

columns.name: CityTier
columns.description: Categorical city tier (1, 2, or 3) indicating city size/market segment.
columns.rationale: Integer categories 1–3 representing city tiers; used as a categorical feature. No nulls mean every customer has a city tier assigned.

columns.name: WarehouseToHome
columns.description: Distance from the assigned warehouse to the customer's home in kilometers.
columns.rationale: Unit: kilometers (km). Nullable: null means distance not available for that customer. Range (5–127 km) enforces plausible warehouse distance values and prevents erroneous outliers.

columns.name: PreferredPaymentMode
columns.description: Customer's preferred payment method (e.g., Credit Card, UPI, Cash on Delivery).
columns.rationale: Allowed values constrained to known payment methods; spellings were unified. Treat this column as categorical; it may be predictive of churn behavior.

columns.name: Gender
columns.description: Customer gender (Male or Female) — protected attribute.
columns.rationale: Protected column — allowed values are ['Female','Male']. This attribute is not recommended as an input feature for production models without a documented fairness review and legal/ethics approval.

columns.name: HourSpendOnApp
columns.description: Average number of hours the customer spends on the app/website (per day).
columns.rationale: Unit: hours (per day). Nullable: null means usage time wasn't recorded. Range 0–5 hours is enforced by cleaning; modelers may cap or transform this field as needed.

columns.name: NumberOfDeviceRegistered
columns.description: Number of devices the customer has registered with their account.
columns.rationale: Integer count of devices (1–6). No nulls. Use as numerical or ordinal feature; values outside the range indicate data issues.

columns.name: PreferedOrderCat
columns.description: Customer's most frequently ordered product category in the last month.
columns.rationale: Canonicalized product category for last month's orders. Treat as categorical input; categories were unified (e.g., 'Mobile Phone' spelling standardized).

columns.name: SatisfactionScore
columns.description: Customer-reported satisfaction on a 1-to-5 scale (higher is better).
columns.rationale: Ordinal integer 1–5. Use as ordinal or numeric input. No nulls; 1 indicates lowest satisfaction and 5 highest.

columns.name: MaritalStatus
columns.description: Customer marital status (Divorced, Married, or Single) — protected attribute.
columns.rationale: Protected column — values are ['Divorced','Married','Single']. Do not use as a feature without approval since it is sensitive.

columns.name: NumberOfAddress
columns.description: Number of delivery addresses the customer has saved.
columns.rationale: Integer count of saved addresses (1–22). No nulls; use as numeric feature, and note the upper bound to detect anomalies.

columns.name: Complain
columns.description: Binary flag indicating if the customer raised any complaint in the last month (1=yes, 0=no).
columns.rationale: Binary flag (0/1) indicating recent complaints; no nulls. This is a strong behavioral signal of churn and should be treated as a feature.

columns.name: OrderAmountHikeFromlastYear
columns.description: Percent change in the customer's order amount versus last year (percentage points).
columns.rationale: Unit: percent. Nullable: null means we don't have a reliable year-over-year change for that customer. Range 11–26 (percentage points) reflects cleaned values; treat as a percent (not a fraction) when engineering features.

columns.name: CouponUsed
columns.description: Count of coupons the customer used in the last month.
columns.rationale: Count of coupons used last month. Nullable: null means usage data missing — imputation or a 'missing' indicator is the modeler's responsibility.

columns.name: OrderCount
columns.description: Number of orders the customer placed in the last month.
columns.rationale: Number of orders in last month. Nullable: null indicates missing order count; modelers must decide how to handle these cases.

columns.name: DaySinceLastOrder
columns.description: Days since the customer's most recent order.
columns.rationale: Unit: days. Nullable: null means last-order date not recorded. Range 0–46 days; higher values indicate longer inactivity and are predictive of churn.

columns.name: CashbackAmount
columns.description: Average cashback amount the customer received in the last month (USD).
columns.rationale: Unit: USD (dollars). Not nullable. Range 0.00–324.99 USD; this monetary amount is in USD and should be treated as continuous currency.

assumptions: CashbackAmount and any monetary amounts are expressed in US dollars (USD), not cents.
OrderAmountHikeFromlastYear is expressed in percentage points (e.g., 20 means a 20% increase), not a fraction between 0 and 1.
Nulls listed in the contract were intentionally kept by the cleaning crew for the modelling team to impute or otherwise handle; imputation is the modelling crew's responsibility.
